The salary map encodes a dual structure: player utility and positional scarcity. Each player’s utility is derived from their projected points normalized by salary, forming a rank-weighted function. Positional scarcity is modeled as an inverse ratio of salary-to-points, indicating how rare high-value players are in a given slot. These primitives form a constrained optimization problem where the objective is to maximize total utility under a fixed salary cap. The failure mode occurs when the utility function becomes non-monotonic due to extreme salary inflation or poor projection accuracy. Dualities emerge between the scalar utility and vectorized scarcity indices, enabling cross-layer validation. The system must avoid overfitting to historical data by enforcing robustness through conformal prediction intervals.
